title: Tenant affinity enforcement & legal-jurisdiction routing for analytics ingest
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Console backend and ingestion pipelines currently accept usage events and tenant metadata without enforcing per-tenant legal-jurisdiction constraints. This leads to cross-region replication of sensitive telemetry for tenants that require data to remain in specific jurisdictions. Goal: Implement a tenant-affinity enforcement layer in the ingest path plus routing controls in the analytics pipeline to ensure events from jurisdiction-bound tenants are only persisted (or replicated) to permitted regions or are held in a quarantined channel for manual review.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Ingest API (console-backend) rejects or routes writes when tenant_jurisdiction metadata conflicts with target region and returns a clear HTTP 409 with remediation guidance.

2) Quarantine Kafka topic is created (analytics.quarantine.<region>) and accepts flagged messages with a standardized reason-code schema; monitoring alerts fire on any non-empty quarantine with >1% of writes.
3) Cross-region mirror jobs respect tenant-level allowlist: tenants with 'residency:region' do not get mirrored out of their region; verification via end-to-end test against staging clusters passes.
4) Per-tenant residency watermark metric is emitted (console.metrics.residency_watermark) and visible on the regional usage dashboard with <1min lag in steady-state.
5) Rollout includes canary in staging -> us-east-1 -> eu-west-1 with automated rollback on policy violations or spike in latencies above 150ms on ingest API.
6) Security team signs off on KMS usage for quarantined data and audit trail requirements are met (audit events persisted for 365 days).

notes: Implementation plan: 1) Add tenant metadata enforcement hook in console-backend (lightweight, feature-flagged). 2) Create quarantine Kafka topics per region with TTL and KMS-encryption. 3) Update kafka-mirror connectors to consult ConfigStore allowlist and skip mirror for bound tenants. 4) Emit residency_watermark and quarantine_rate metrics; add dashboards and alerts. 5) Run canary and staged rollout with automated validation suite.

Design trade-offs: Rejecting writes preserves strong residency but creates a poor UX and potential data loss for customers whose instrumentation mis-tags jurisdiction. Quarantine plus notification chosen as default; provide tenant-level opt-in for strict reject mode for customers that require absolute in-region denial.

Operational concerns: Quarantine growth could become unbounded during region outages; plan includes backpressure signals to console-backend (429) when per-region quarantine queue exceeds 1M messages, plus eviction policy and support ticketing automation.

Testing strategy: End-to-end tests using synthetic tenants with 'residency=EU' and 'residency=US', verified against staging mirrors; property-based tests for watermark semantics; integration tests for audit log generation.
